baseline.label: Legacy regional beach guide
baseline.notes: Useful static inventory and map, but no official water-quality notices, hazard overrides, daily decision layer, transparent score, source-health states, or dedicated beach landing pages.

checks.description: Combines BeachGuard, NWS, NOAA buoy, and weather inputs in one endpoint.
Catalog covers at least 50 Michigan Great Lakes shoreline destinations.
Search, lake and trait filters, sorting, map, and on-device distance are implemented.
An automatically seasonal daily ranking converts raw conditions into a useful shortlist.
Closures, advisories, and hazards override scores and ranking eligibility.
No-alert and unavailable states explicitly avoid implying a recent test or all-clear.
Observation freshness, station identity, distance, source links, and source health are visible.
Upstream calls run in parallel with timeouts and cache policy.
Missing, incomplete, or stale NOAA observations produce N/A rather than fallback points and are excluded from rankings.
Each source has an explicit unavailable state and the UI keeps official-source fallbacks.
Responsive layouts, focus treatment, reduced-motion handling, labels, and semantic controls are present.
Loading, empty, error, geolocation denial, no-JavaScript, and dialog states are handled.
The experience uses a credited, public-domain National Park Service shoreline photograph.
Main and daily pages have canonical metadata, concise answers, breadcrumbs, and FAQ structured data.
Every catalog entry has a canonical, structured, unique detail page in a dedicated sitemap.
Tools, Great Lakes hub, homepage copy, robots, and llms.txt point search systems and people to the report.
Daily ranking is active May 15–September 15 and pauses cleanly while the explorer stays live.
Search, Near Me, detail-open, and daily-pick interactions emit analytics events.
A documented KPI scorecard defines launch, adoption, retention, discovery, and truth targets.
